--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -290,10 +290,23 @@
-def b58encode_check(
-    v: Union[str, bytes], alphabet: bytes = BITCOIN_ALPHABET
-) -> bytes:
-    """
-    Encode a string using Base58 with a 4 character checksum
-    """
-    v = scrub_input(v)
-
-    digest = sha256(sha256(v).digest()).digest()
-    return b58encode(v + digest[:4], alphabet=alphabet)
+# Empty hash object to copy from: a copy skips the digest lookup and
+# initialisation that every sha256() call performs
+_SHA256 = sha256()
+
+
+def _checksum(v: bytes) -> bytes:
+    # First four bytes of sha256(sha256(v))
+    inner = _SHA256.copy()
+    inner.update(v)
+    outer = _SHA256.copy()
+    outer.update(inner.digest())
+    return outer.digest()[:4]
+
+
+def b58encode_check(
+    v: Union[str, bytes], alphabet: bytes = BITCOIN_ALPHABET
+) -> bytes:
+    """
+    Encode a string using Base58 with a 4 character checksum
+    """
+    v = scrub_input(v)
+
+    return b58encode(v + _checksum(v), alphabet=alphabet)

--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -323,3 +323,1 @@
-    digest = sha256(sha256(result).digest()).digest()
-
-    if check != digest[:4]:
+    if check != _checksum(result):

actions.reason: The one candidate tried, building the Base58Check checksum by copying a prebuilt empty sha256 object instead of calling sha256() four times per round trip, made things worse when measured: check_ir ratio 1.0037, encode_ir and decode_ir both 1.0010. Its outputs matched the parent byte for byte. The extra method calls cost more than the hash setup they saved. It has been reverted, so the tree matches the parent. The other ideas left (caching decode steps per length, inlining scrub_input) are estimated at about 0.2% each, which is below the 1% minimum, so no change was submitted.

journal.text:
Test agent here. Session on base58-py, Base58Check path. Same bytes out was the bar. I tried one idea. Instead of calling sha256() four times per round trip, I copied a prebuilt empty sha256 object for the checksum.

Outputs matched the parent byte for byte. The numbers went the wrong way. check_ir ratio 1.0037, against a required 0.9900. encode_ir and decode_ir both came in at 1.0010. The sandbox rejected it as no improvement. Guards and both builds were fine. I reverted the edits and submitted nothing.

What I believe now. Hash setup is not where this code spends its time. The copy() call plus the extra method lookups cost more than a fresh sha256() saved. Small tide, wrong direction.

Next I will profile check_ir before editing anything. I want to see how much time sits in the big-int divmod loop versus the checksum. Not measured yet. Then I pick the larger cost and try one change there.
